transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-13 15:00 EDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan Blake, Priya Shah (Redwood) 	6 Jennifer Park, David Liu, Maria Gonzalez (Walnut Financial)
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. I'm Jordan, I'm the AE on the account, Priya is our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Jennifer: Hi, Jennifer here 	6 CTO.
[00:00:12] David: David, head of ops.
[00:00:14] Maria: Maria, compliance.
[00:00:18] Jordan: Great. We're here to understand your residency and compliance constraints and see where Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private fit. We'll keep it practical 	6 timelines, success criteria, and any must-haves.
[00:00:35] Priya: Hi all. I will probably jump in with a few technical clarifications 	6 infra, encryption, logging details.
[00:00:45] Jennifer: Awesome. To start high level 	6 Walnut is building a customer-facing virtual assistant and a KYC automation pipeline. We need to run new inference workloads that touch PII and account data. Our security team says data must remain in-region for EU users, and for US financial accounts we have stricter logging rules.
[00:01:05] Jordan: Understood. Can you clarify the EU in-region requirement 	6 is it GDPR residency (data must not leave EU) or just processing locality for audit?
[00:01:16] Maria: It's GDPR processing locality. We need EU customer data to be processed and stored only in EU data centers for now. Also for certain records we have a 7-year retention rule, but audit logs must be redacted for customer identifiers in logs.
[00:01:32] David: Also we're evaluating vendors 	6 cost matters, but the dealbreaker is any logs that contain raw account numbers or full SSNs leaving our VPC. We need either log scrubbing before it leaves, or no log export.
[00:01:46] Priya: Okay that's helpful. On Redwood's side: we offer Hosted (multi-region but by default logs and telemetry are stored in our control plane), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in region with optional network isolation), and Private (customer-managed control plane / VPC or on-prem). For GDPR EU-residency we can pin processing to EU regions either via Dedicated capacity or Private. For Hosted we can do region-aware routing, but control plane telemetry lives in Redwood unless you opt for our Private deployment.
[00:02:20] Jordan: Quick note 	6 our Hosted offering has strong controls but if you require full data plane residency and control plane segregation, Dedicated with VPC peering or Private is recommended.
[00:02:33] Maria: Can you elaborate on logging 	6 what exactly you capture by default? We cannot have request-level payloads or PII in logs.
[00:02:42] Priya: Default telemetry captures request metadata, latency, token counts, and anonymized error traces. By default we do not persist full prompts in analytics unless you opt-in for debug logging. That said, some debug traces can contain payloads and we recommend redact-before-ship for regulated workloads.
[00:03:00] Jennifer: Is there an option to disable analytics entirely for a Dedicated pool?
[00:03:05] Priya: Yes. For Dedicated you can disable control-plane telemetry, and for Private you control the control plane entirely. For Dedicated we can also enable local logging only, and set a retention policy 	6 e.g., logs auto-expire after X days and sensitive fields are redacted at the source using our SDK hooks.
[00:03:22] David: SDK hooks 	6 are those client-side? We want to perform redaction before any data leaves our app tier.
[00:03:27] Priya: Correct. We have pre-send hooks in our SDK so you can strip, hash, or tokenise PII. Many banks run a pre-processing step that pseudonymizes account numbers before sending.
[00:03:38] Maria: What about encryption? KMS integrations? We must ensure keys are customer managed ideally HSM-backed.
[00:03:45] Priya: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted customers we offer encrypt-at-rest with Redwood-managed keys, but you can request CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for an additional contract in Dedicated.
[00:03:59] Jordan: To be explicit: if Walnut requires HSM-backed KMS and full log isolation, Private is the cleanest path. Dedicated can meet many requirements but will require contractual addendums.
[00:04:12] Jennifer: Good to know. For GDPR we also need to know about subprocessors and data transfers 	6 do you have SCCs?
[00:04:18] Jordan: Yes, we have standard contractual clauses and data processing addendum we can share. We'll include SCCs and our list of subprocessors in the packet.
[00:04:25] Maria: Also incident reporting SLA 	6 72 hours? 24 hours? For financial regs we need 24 hour breach notification in some jurisdictions.
[00:04:33] Jordan: Our standard is 72 hours, but enterprise contracts can include 24-hour notification. We'll surface that with legal.
[00:04:40] [00:04:40] Speaker 1: (mumble) can we see a sample log?
[00:04:43] Priya: Yes, I'll share sample logs with redaction examples.
[00:04:47] [00:05:00] David: Let's talk about model fallbacks and caching 	6 we don't want raw customer text cached in a shared KV cache across tenants. How is KV cache handled?
[00:05:08] Priya: Good question. Our runtime supports per-tenant KV cache and optional in-memory only mode. In Dedicated/Private we can pin KV cache to the customer's instance and evict after each session, or run cache encryption keys scoped per-customer. For Hosted, default caching is multi-tenant and not suitable for your requirement unless we enable tenant isolation.
[00:05:30] Jennifer: Is there an option to disable caching entirely?
[00:05:33] Priya: Yes, caching can be disabled at the route or model level. The tradeoff is throughput and cost 	6 you'll see higher latency and token cost if cache is off.
[00:05:45] Maria: That tradeoff is acceptable for the account-level PII flows. For anonymized assistant prompts maybe we can enable cache.
[00:05:53] Jordan: Timelines 	6 what's your expected pilot and go-live window?
[00:05:57] Jennifer: We'd like to pilot within 4	66 weeks and go-to-prod in three months depending on contract and security sign-off.
[00:06:05] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. Priya, any questions about compliance frameworks?
[00:06:10] Priya: A couple 	6 does Walnut have HIPAA scope for any of this? Even if not, if you have any PHI the platform would need BAAs and special handling.
[00:06:20] Maria: Not HIPAA. It's financial PII, so GLBA-ish controls plus SOC2 Type II are our checklist. We will expect SOC2 reports and pen test results.
[00:06:29] Jordan: We'll attach our SOC2 Type II report and recent penetration test summary.
[00:06:33] [00:06:40] Jennifer: Regarding region constraints: EU users must be processed in EU and logs must remain in-region. For US users, we need to ensure data for certain regulated products stays in specific US regions (East vs West). Can Redwood route by policy?
[00:06:53] Priya: Yes, smart routing is a core feature 	6 requests can be routed by region, latency, or customer tier. For Dedicated you'd provision pools in each region and the router will direct requests appropriately. For Private you'd host the control plane in your region.
[00:07:07] David: How does model fallback work if regional pool is down? We can't have EU requests routed to a US pool.
[00:07:13] Priya: We can configure no-cross-region fallback for those routes. The router's policy can be set to fail closed if compatible capacity is not available. That will increase risk of transient errors, but keeps compliance.
[00:07:27] Maria: How about audit logs and who can see them? We must restrict access to logs with PII and have RBAC.
[00:07:34] Priya: RBAC is available in Redwood Console. For Dedicated/Private you can integrate with your SSO (SAML/SCIM) and define roles. Audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) and we support filtering/redaction.
[00:07:48] Jennifer: Speaking of SSO, does Redwood support SAML-based SSO and SCIM provisioning?
[00:07:52] Jordan: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM are supported for Enterprise plans. We'll attach the SSO integration guide.
[00:07:59] [00:08:10] David: Performance 	6 we'll need to run a 48hr benchmark on our sample workload. Can Redwood give isolated Dedicated capacity for that?
[00:08:18] Priya: Yes, we can allocate a Dedicated pool for benchmarks. We'll also provide guidance on batch sizing and quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize so you can see real cost vs latency numbers.
[00:08:29] Maria: For logging retention, do you support automatic redaction regex rules?
[00:08:34] Priya: We do. You can supply regex or a redaction script. We have pre-built scrubbing for credit-card-like patterns, SSN-like patterns, and account numbers 	6 though you'll want to validate against your formats.
[00:08:48] Jennifer: Are there any known limitations for on-prem/private? Does Redwood Private require specific kubernetes versions?
[00:08:54] Priya: Private supports a set of supported K8s versions 	6 we'll include an install matrix. For air-gapped deployments we have a support package. Some runtime optimizations rely on specific drivers (NVIDIA driver versions) but our ops team will provide the checklist.
[00:09:10] Jordan: Cost signals 	6 Alex (pricing) will follow up but roughly Dedicated is a capacity commit (monthly/annual) and Private has platform fee plus infra. Hosted per-token is easiest to start but may not meet compliance.
[00:09:23] David: Understood. A few more subtle items 	6 can we get an option to redact logs at the edge (load balancer) before hitting Redwood?
[00:09:31] Priya: Absolutely. Many customers run an edge proxy or our SDK prehooks to scrub PII before the payload reaches Redwood. We'll share a reference architecture.
[00:09:42] Maria: Also we need to confirm that debug logs are off by default and that any redaction step is enforced as part of deploy.
[00:09:49] Priya: Debug mode is opt-in only. For Dedicated/Private we can enforce settings via policy and disable debug across the fleet.
[00:09:58] [00:10:10] Jennifer: Ok let's capture immediate asks: 1) SOC2 + ISO report + SCC and DPA 2) Sample redacted logs and redaction recommendations 3) Benchmark slot and Dedicated capacity quote 4) SSO/SCIM integration guide and install matrix 5) Contractual breach notification terms.
[00:10:28] Jordan: We'll deliver that packet. Priya will lead the technical follow-up.
[00:10:34] Priya: I'll propose two times for the 2-hour deep dive that includes a bench: Wed 2026-05-20 and Fri 2026-05-22.
[00:10:41] David: Either is fine.
[00:10:44] Maria: Prefer Wed.
[00:10:47] Jordan: Great. Anything else?
[00:10:50] Jennifer: One minor item 	6 model explainability. Regulators may ask for why a decision was made. What level of deterministic tracing do you provide?
[00:11:00] Priya: We provide structured output and token-level traces that can be captured in audit logs. For production you can enable minimal explainability artifacts 	6 e.g., top-k tokens and model scores 	6 but avoid storing raw prompts. We also recommend a rules-based guard for high-risk decisions.
[00:11:17] [00:11:30] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) will you share cost estimates for caching off vs on?
[00:11:34] Priya: Yes, we'll include a cost delta example in the packet and show per-token cost with caching on vs off.
[00:11:41] Jordan: Quick recap 	6 Walnut needs EU in-region processing, per-route log redaction, KMS/HSM for keys, SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and a 2	66 week pilot. Preferred path seems Dedicated with potential Private for contractually strict controls. We'll send legal/security packet and schedule the deep technical bench.
[00:12:02] Jennifer: That matches my notes. Thank you.
[00:12:05] Maria: Thanks, Jordan.
[00:12:07] David: Thanks everyone.
[00:12:10] Jordan: We'll follow up with the doc bundle and the calendar invite.
[00:12:15] [END OF INTRO 	6 remainder of call is Q&A and scoping]
[00:12:30] [00:12:30] Priya: Diving in 	6 sample architecture idea: app tier in EU -> edge proxy redacts PII -> VPC peering to Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 -> local logging to your SIEM. Here's a quick link to a reference diagram: https://redwood.example/security/arch/walnut-eu-ref (will send official)
[00:13:05] David: For the edge proxy, we run a Fargate sidecar 	6 do you have examples?
[00:13:09] Priya: Yes we have a Fargate + lambda example. I'll attach.
[00:13:15] [00:14:00] Jennifer: On retention: can logs be auto-purged at 30 days for EU customers, but 7 years for audit datasets? We need flexible retention per dataset.
[00:14:10] Priya: Retention policies are configurable by log type and route in Dedicated/Private. Some audit datasets that are legally required can be exported to your S3 and we can set lifecycle policies.
[00:14:24] Maria: If exported to S3, encryption keys must be customer-managed.
[00:14:29] Priya: Supported.
[00:14:32] [00:15:00] David: Any gotchas around inference determinism for audits? If we run the same prompt twice we might get different outputs.
[00:15:09] Priya: LLMs are probabilistic by nature. For auditability we recommend deterministic sampling (temperature = 0) or using a snapshot model version pinned 	6 we support model version pinning for reproducible outputs. Also store the seed and model config in the audit artifact.
[00:15:27] Jordan: OK. We're approaching the last third of the call 	6 quick logistics: pricing and contract owner who will sign?
[00:15:36] Jennifer: Contracts will be handled by our procurement team; I'll introduce the buyer if we progress. Timeline still 4	66 weeks pilot.
[00:15:45] Jordan: Great. Priya, anything else to capture?
[00:15:48] Priya: I'll include the install matrix, redaction examples, and a sample benchmarking playbook. Also will note recommended quantization and batching settings to get to target latency.
[00:16:02] [00:16:30] Jennifer: One more question 	6 isolation of model weights: do you host open models or provide a mechanism to bring-your-own-model?
[00:16:37] Priya: We host curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. For Dedicated/Private you can BYOM (bring your own model) and we can host it inside your private pool, subject to licensing.
[00:16:50] Maria: Any concerns about model training data leakage? We don't plan to fine-tune on customer PII.
[00:16:56] Priya: We don't use customer data to train public models. For Private you fully control training. For Hosted we have strict isolation. We'll include our data usage policy in the packet.
[00:17:10] [00:18:00] Jordan: Alright let's record the deliverables and owners (we'll send as follow-up too). Thanks everybody 	6 we'll be in touch with the packet by Friday.
[00:18:12] Jennifer: Thanks.
[00:18:14] David: Thanks.
[00:18:16] Maria: Bye.
[00:51:30] [Call ends 	6 brief wrapups in chat where Jordan posts links to docs]
